question: In the 2010 cross-sectional survey of community-based older companion dogs (mean age 11.67 years) that applied a provisional diagnosis based on 27 significant behavioural items, what was the estimated prevalence of canine cognitive dysfunction, and what percentage of dogs had actually been diagnosed with CCD by a veterinarian?
answer: Estimated prevalence 14.2%, versus only 1.9% diagnosed by a veterinarian.

evidence.title: Under diagnosis of canine cognitive dysfunction: a cross-sectional survey of older companion dogs.
evidence.quote: Using a provisional diagnosis based on 27 significant behavioural items, the prevalence rate of CCD was estimated to be 14.2%. This was in contrast with only 1.9% diagnosed with CCD by a veterinarian.

question: In the 2010 cross-sectional survey on under-diagnosis of canine cognitive dysfunction in older companion dogs, how many items did the owner questionnaire contain, how many behavioural domains did it cover, and how many of the eligible responses were used for the analysis?
answer: An 84-item questionnaire covering six behavioural domains; a randomly selected half (n=497) of the 957 eligible responses was analysed.

evidence.title: Under diagnosis of canine cognitive dysfunction: a cross-sectional survey of older companion dogs.
evidence.quote: An 84-item questionnaire was used to obtain information across six behavioural domains. Of the eligible survey responses obtained (n=957) a randomly selected one-half (n=497) was used for this study.

question: In the Dog Aging Project study that applied a minimally modified canine cognitive dysfunction rating scale to a nationwide cohort of 15,019 companion dogs, by what percentage did the odds of CCD increase with each additional year of age when controlling for all other characteristics?
answer: The odds of CCD increased 52% with each additional year of age.

evidence.title: Evaluation of cognitive function in the Dog Aging Project: associations with baseline canine characteristics.
evidence.quote: When controlling for all other characteristics, the odds of CCD increased 52% with each additional year of age.

question: In the Dog Aging Project cross-sectional analysis of cognitive function in 15,019 companion dogs, how many times higher were the odds of canine cognitive dysfunction in dogs reported as not active compared with very active dogs of the same age, health status, breed type and sterilization status?

evidence.title: Evaluation of cognitive function in the Dog Aging Project: associations with baseline canine characteristics.
evidence.quote: Among dogs of the same age, health status, breed type, and sterilization status, odds of CCD were 6.47 times higher in dogs who were not active compared to those who were very active.

question: In the Dog Aging Project cross-sectional study of physical activity and cognitive dysfunction in companion dogs aged 6-18 years, how many dogs were included in the sample and how many of them had scores over the clinical threshold for CCD?
answer: 11,574 companion dogs, of whom 287 had scores over the clinical CCD threshold.

evidence.title: Associations between physical activity and cognitive dysfunction in older companion dogs: results from the Dog Aging Project.
evidence.quote: Our sample included 11,574 companion dogs enrolled through the Dog Aging Project, of whom 287 had scores over the clinical threshold for CCD.

question: As described in the 2025 study evaluating blood-based diagnostic biomarkers for canine cognitive dysfunction syndrome in 77 dogs, how many questions does the Canine Cognitive Dysfunction Rating Scale (CCDR) contain, across how many domains, on what response scale, and into which categories does it classify dogs?
answer: 13 questions across four domains, each scored on a 1-5 scale; dogs are categorised as normal, at-risk, or CDS.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Blood-Based Diagnostic Biomarkers for Canine Cognitive Dysfunction Syndrome.
evidence.quote: The CCDR consists of 13 questions across four domains, with responses scored on a 1-5 scale, categorizing dogs as normal, at-risk, or CDS.

question: In the 2025 study of 77 dogs that measured plasma Aβ40, Aβ42 and GFAP and serum NfL alongside the CCDR, CADES and CCAS questionnaires, which biomarker was significantly elevated with cognitive dysfunction stage across all three questionnaires, and what ROC areas under the curve did it achieve against each questionnaire?
answer: Serum neurofilament light chain (NfL) only; AUCs of 0.763 (CCDR), 0.722 (CADES) and 0.777 (CCAS). Aβ40, Aβ42 and GFAP were not significantly associated with CDS stage.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Blood-Based Diagnostic Biomarkers for Canine Cognitive Dysfunction Syndrome.
evidence.quote: While Aβ40, Aβ42, and GFAP were not significantly associated with CDS stage, serum NfL levels were elevated (p < 0.05) across all questionnaires. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses showed areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.763 (CCDR), 0.722 (CADES), and 0.777 (CCAS), with cut-off values around 18.28-43.13 pg/mL.

notes: Quote copied from the abstract as stored in the corpus, including the p markup.

question: In the 2022 study that quantified cognitive impairment in an aging pet dog population using cognitive testing, the CADES and CCDR questionnaires, and plasma neurofilament light chain, how many dogs and how many breeds were recruited, and what was the age range?
answer: 39 dogs from 15 breeds, aged 9.3 to 15.3 years.

evidence.title: Use of Cognitive Testing, Questionnaires, and Plasma Biomarkers to Quantify Cognitive Impairment in an Aging Pet Dog Population.
evidence.quote: Thirty-nine dogs from fifteen breeds were recruited (9.3 to 15.3 years).

question: In the 2025 systematic review of enriched diets and nutraceuticals for enhancing cognitive function in aged dogs and cats, how many clinical trials were reviewed, how were they split between canine and feline trials, and what publication period did they span?
answer: 30 studies (27 canine and 2 feline trials), published between 2002 and 2023.

evidence.title: Enhancing cognitive functions in aged dogs and cats: a systematic review of enriched diets and nutraceuticals.
evidence.quote: A total of 30 studies (27 canine and 2 feline trials) published between 2002 and 2023 were reviewed.

notes: The abstract counts (27 + 2) do not sum to 30; the answer reports the figures exactly as stated in the source.

question: In the 2001 cohort study of dogs aged 11 to 14 years (29 sexually intact males, 63 spayed females and 47 castrated males) whose owners were interviewed twice, 12 to 18 months apart, about impairment in four behavioural categories, which group was significantly less likely to progress from mild impairment (one category) to severe impairment (two or more categories)?
answer: Sexually intact male dogs were significantly less likely than neutered dogs to progress from mild to severe impairment.

evidence.title: Effect of gonadectomy on subsequent development of age-related cognitive impairment in dogs.
evidence.quote: Sexually intact male dogs were significantly less likely than neutered dogs to progress from mild impairment (i.e., impairment in 1 category) to severe impairment (i.e., impairment in > or = 2 categories) during the time between the first and second interviews.

question: In the longitudinal beagle study of long-term antioxidant-fortified food and behavioral enrichment, 48 aged dogs (9-12 years) were assigned to four cognitively equivalent groups of 12; after one year, what pattern did the improvements in size discrimination and reversal learning largely reflect, and what did the authors conclude about antioxidant effectiveness?
answer: Improvements largely reflected the combined treatment group (fortified food plus enriched environment); the authors concluded antioxidant effectiveness depends on behavioral and environmental experience.

evidence.title: Long-term treatment with antioxidants and a program of behavioral enrichment reduces age-dependent impairment in discrimination and reversal learning in beagle dogs.
evidence.quote: Both tasks were also improved by both the fortified food and the behavioral enrichment. However, in both instances the treatment effects largely reflected improved performance in the combined treatment group. These results suggest that the effectiveness of antioxidants in attenuating age-dependent cognitive decline is dependent on behavioral and environmental experience.

evidence.title: Long-term treatment with antioxidants and a program of behavioral enrichment reduces age-dependent impairment in discrimination and reversal learning in beagle dogs.
evidence.quote: Baseline performance on a battery of cognitive tests was used to assign 48 aged dogs (9-12 years) into four cognitively equivalent groups, of 12 animals per group: Group CC (control food-control environment), group CE (control food-enriched environment); Group AC (antioxidant fortified food-control environment); Group AE (fortified food-enriched environment).

question: In the 1996 study of 20 canines (11 purebred beagles and 9 mongrels) tested on a battery of six cognitive tasks, which task showed the strongest association between beta-amyloid deposition and performance deficits after controlling for age-related increases in beta-amyloid, what was its correlation coefficient, and were neurofibrillary tangles detected?
answer: Discrimination learning, r = .80 (reversal learning r = .65, spatial learning r = .54); no neurofibrillary tangles were detected.

evidence.title: Beta-amyloid accumulation correlates with cognitive dysfunction in the aged canine.
evidence.quote: Controlling for age-related increases in beta-amyloid, we observed that increased beta-amyloid deposition is strongly associated with deficits on Discrimination learning (r = .80), Reversal learning (r = .65), and Spatial learning (r = .54) but not the other tasks.

evidence.title: Beta-amyloid accumulation correlates with cognitive dysfunction in the aged canine.
evidence.quote: No neurofibrillary tangles were detected. beta-Amyloid was also associated with the processes of many neurons and with blood vessels.

question: In the 2025 comparison of 21 aged dogs from the placebo arm of a randomized controlled trial with 17 aged dogs from an observational longitudinal study, which owner-completed cognitive questionnaire showed a strong, significant improvement in the placebo cohort after 6 months, and which questionnaire did the authors conclude is more robust against the caregiver placebo effect?
answer: CADES improved significantly in the placebo cohort (g = 0.76, p = 0.021) while CCDR showed no change; the authors concluded CCDR is more robust against caregiver placebo effect than CADES.

evidence.title: Quantifying placebo and trial participation effects on cognitive outcome measures in aging dogs.
evidence.quote: A strong (g = 0.76), significant (p = 0.021) improvement in CADES was observed in the placebo cohort after 6 months, while no changes were detected with CCDR.

evidence.title: Quantifying placebo and trial participation effects on cognitive outcome measures in aging dogs.
evidence.quote: We conclude that study context influences remotely delivered owner assessments and CCDR is more robust against caregiver placebo effect in RCTs than CADES.
